name: Treaty with the Chippewa, Red Lake and Pembina Bands, 1863 (Treaty of Old Crossing)
nations: Pembina Band of Ojibwe (today within the Turtle Mountain, White Earth and Little Shell communities)
promises: Article 3: $20,000 a year for twenty years, paid per capita after an enrollment, with up to $5,000 a year that the President could direct to agriculture, education and goods.
Article 4: no punishment for past offences, and a fund to settle traders' depredation claims, with any balance added to the bands' annuities.
Article 5: payments to chiefs out of the annuities, $500 a year for agriculture and $5,000 for a road from Leech Lake to Red Lake.
Article 8: a 160-acre homestead within the ceded area for each qualifying adult mixed-blood relative.

breaches.what: The Commission valued the lands ceded in the Red River Valley and northwestern Minnesota at $3,369,726 and found the consideration unconscionable; the treaty-date value of what the United States actually paid was $512,518.43.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Red Lake, Pembina and White Earth Bands v. United States, Dockets 18-A, 113 and 191, 9 Ind. Cl. Comm. 457 (1961)

source.title: Red Lake, Pembina and White Earth Bands v. United States, Dockets 18-A, 113, 191, Opinion of the Commission, October 5, 1961
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

compensation: The Commission's amended final award of April 24, 1964 gave $2,034,889.56 ($3,369,726 less $635,774.87 paid on the claim and $699,061.57 in gratuitous offsets): $1,797,761.74 to the Red Lake Band and $237,127.82 to the Pembina Band.
today: The Red Lake Nation holds the lands around Red Lake that it did not cede in 1863.

openQuestions: The 1958 valuation opinion (6 Ind. Cl. Comm. 247, OSU pointers 268 and 200) that first held the consideration unconscionable and gives the acreage was not opened; the acreage ceded is left out until it is.
The 1863 treaty was amended by the Senate and supplemented by the treaty of April 12, 1864 (13 Stat. 689); the supplement's changes to the annuities were not compared.

The Red Lake Nation's own account of the treaty (redlakenation.org, Red Lake Nation News coverage of Old Crossing commemorations) was not opened. Turtle Mountain's later claims in Docket 113 (1970-1978) concern the Pembina share and are a lead.
The 'today' sentence is general and should be tied to a dated Red Lake source.
